explanation.en: Danger warning signs are equilateral triangles: white or yellow ground, red border, black symbol, point up.

stem.en: What is the standard shape of a danger warning sign?

explanation.en: Outside built-up areas warning signs stand far enough ahead (commonly 150 to 250 m) that drivers can react in time.

en.b: Well in advance of the hazard

stem.en: Where is a danger warning sign placed relative to the hazard?

explanation.en: Both the double-bend symbol and the slippery-road symbol are danger warnings: triangular, red border.

stem.en: Which two meanings belong to triangular red-bordered signs? (two correct)

explanation.en: Give way is an inverted triangle; STOP is an octagon with STOP in white on red.

en.c: Give way is an inverted triangle, STOP is octagonal

stem.en: How do the GIVE WAY and STOP signs differ in shape?

explanation.en: The yellow diamond marks a priority road: you have priority at every intersection until the end-of-priority sign.

en.a: You are on a priority road
en.b: You must stop at every junction

stem.en: What does a yellow diamond sign tell you?

explanation.en: The red-white arrow sign gives priority to oncoming traffic; the blue-red square gives you priority over oncoming vehicles on a narrow section.

en.b: Round red-white yields to oncoming traffic; square blue-red keeps your priority

stem.en: On a narrow road, what is the difference between the round and square priority signs?

explanation.en: The St. Andrew's cross marks a level crossing, placed at the crossing itself.

en.a: Level crossing ahead or at the crossing

stem.en: What does the X-shaped St. Andrew's cross indicate?

questions.article: Vienna Convention, Annex 1, Section A (automatic level crossing with gates)

explanation.en: You must stop when the barrier starts to lower or the red lights flash, and never weave around a lowered barrier.

en.a: Speed up to beat the barrier
en.b: Stop only if a train is visible
en.c: Stop and wait until the barrier rises and lights stop

stem.en: The barrier at a level crossing starts to lower. What do you do?

explanation.en: The three countdown markers show roughly 240 m, 160 m and 80 m to a level crossing outside built-up areas.

en.b: Remaining distance to the level crossing

stem.en: Red-and-white striped posts with three, two and one bars appear before a crossing. What do they mean?

questions.article: Vienna Convention, Annex 4, Section A (prohibition and restriction)

explanation.en: Prohibitory signs are round with a red border (no entry, no overtaking, speed limits).

stem.en: What shape do prohibitory signs have?

explanation.en: The red disc means no entry for all vehicles; the overtaking ban shows two cars side by side, red car over black.

stem.en: What does a plain red disc with a white horizontal bar mean?

explanation.en: A crossed-out number in a red-bordered round sign ends a speed limit; the grey crossed disc ends all prohibitions.

stem.en: Which meanings belong to grey round signs with a diagonal bar? (two correct)

questions.article: Vienna Convention, Annex 4, Section D (mandatory signs)

explanation.en: Mandatory signs are round and blue with a white symbol: they order a direction or behaviour.

stem.en: What shape and colour do mandatory signs have?

explanation.en: A blue round sign with a white arrow orders the direction (e.g. turn right); a blue sign with a white bar orders passing on the indicated side.

en.a: You must follow the indicated direction
en.b: You may ignore it when traffic is light

stem.en: What does a blue round sign with a white arrow require?

explanation.en: Blue round signs also mark compulsory paths: cycle path, footpath, bridle path, or a roundabout to be circled as shown.

stem.en: What does a blue round sign showing a white bicycle mean?

explanation.en: Informative signs are usually rectangular: blue or green for orientation and motorways, with white symbols.

stem.en: What is the typical shape of an informative sign?

explanation.en: Motorway and express-road signs announce special rules (no stopping, no U-turns, minimum speeds where posted).

stem.en: A blue or green rectangular sign with a stylised highway interchange appears. What begins here?

explanation.en: One-way and hospital/first-aid panels are informative: rectangular, guiding rather than ordering.

stem.en: Which two are informative signs? (two correct)

explanation.en: The blue square with a white P marks a place where parking is allowed.

stem.en: What does a blue square sign with a white P mean?

explanation.en: A blue disc with a red border and one red diagonal bar bans parking; two bars (a cross) ban even stopping.

en.a: Parking is prohibited, stopping briefly is allowed

stem.en: What does a blue round sign with a red border and a single red diagonal bar mean?

questions.article: Vienna Convention, Annex 6 with Annex 7 panels

explanation.en: Panels under parking signs limit the permission: vehicle categories, time windows, duration, or side of the road.

en.b: Parking is allowed only as the panel describes

stem.en: A small rectangular panel sits under a parking sign. What does it do?

explanation.en: Additional panels (H) are small rectangles placed under a sign to qualify it: distance, length, time, vehicle class.

en.a: They qualify the sign above them
en.b: They cancel the sign above them

stem.en: What is the purpose of a small rectangular panel under a traffic sign?

explanation.en: '800 m' extends the rule's reach; a time plate like '8-18h' restricts the rule to those hours.

en.c: The distance or time the sign applies to

stem.en: A panel under a no-parking sign reads '8-18h'. What does it mean?

explanation.en: Symbol panels restrict a sign to a vehicle class (e.g. lorries) or exempt one (e.g. 'except buses').

en.b: The sign applies only to the pictured vehicle class
en.c: The panel shows the sign designer

stem.en: A lorry symbol appears on the panel under a prohibition sign. What follows?

explanation.en: A continuous centre line bans crossing it (no overtaking, no U-turns across it); a broken line allows crossing when safe.

en.a: You must not cross or straddle it
en.b: You may park on it briefly

stem.en: What does a continuous white centre line require?

questions.article: Vienna Convention, Annex 8 (stop lines and crossings)

explanation.en: The transverse stop line marks where to halt for a STOP sign, red light, or give-way where required.

en.a: The start of a parking bay
en.b: The place to stop when required

stem.en: What is the wide white line across your lane before an intersection for?

explanation.en: Lane arrows channel traffic by direction; zebra stripes mark pedestrian crossings where walkers have priority.

stem.en: Which two markings organise lanes and pedestrian priority? (two correct)

explanation.en: Red means stop, amber (alone after green) means stop unless unable to, green means go when the way is clear.

en.c: Red stops, green allows passage when clear

stem.en: What do the three colours of a traffic light mean in order?

explanation.en: A flashing amber light means proceed with caution: priority rules apply as if the light were absent.

en.a: Proceed carefully, normal priority rules apply
en.c: The lights are broken, ignore all rules

stem.en: The traffic light flashes amber. What do you do?

explanation.en: A red cross above a lane closes it; a green arrow opens it. Reversible lanes switch with traffic flow.

en.b: Red cross closes the lane, green arrow opens it

stem.en: What do signals mounted above individual lanes mean?
